name: Shaul
overview: Shaul was a male Edomite king who succeeded Samlah as ruler over Edom. He originated from Rehoboth on the Euphrates river, indicating his geographical and tribal association within the Edomite lineage. His kingship is noted in the genealogical records of Genesis 36:37.
namesAndTitles: The name Shaul means 'asked' or possibly 'dedicated to God,' reflecting a Hebrew origin and significance. This proper name was not given by God but appears in the biblical genealogical record in Genesis 36:37.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shaul as a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded for Shaul in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shaul's significance lies in his role as a king of Edom, a nation descended from Esau, which situates him within the broader biblical narrative of the nations related to Israel. His reign following Samlah marks a continuation of Edomite leadership during the period recorded in Genesis. This contributes to the understanding of Edom's political history and its place in the biblical genealogies.
